plan.notes: Transcribed 2026-11-12 from the official Southern Utah University 2026-2027 General Catalog (current edition, catoid=28) English - Literature Emphasis program page and its linked official degree map workbook, 'English & English Education Degree Maps (2026-2027)', 'Literature (Campus)' tab, last updated/reviewed August 3, 2026. Semester placement is the university's official sample 4-year campus academic plan (SUU Program Maps, 2026-2027), which the source itself labels a guide only; students confirm specifics in Degree Works with a Student Success Advisor. Every term's courses sum to the map's printed term total (16/14/16/14/15/15/15/15) and the plan to the catalog's printed BA degree total of 120. BA-only program: the catalog prints a single line, Total Credits, BA Degree: 120, which the map matches exactly; no BS option is printed. The catalog's Bachelor of Arts Degree Requirement is 16 foreign-language credits (four semesters of a foreign language, or testing out and purchasing the credits; one semester may also fulfill the General Education Humanities requirement); the map's four LANG rows (1010/1020/2010/2020 at 4 credits each) satisfy it exactly. The catalog's General Education block prints only Core Course Requirements (12+ credits) and Breadth Area Requirements (16+ credits) with 'See General Education for course options'; the map's GE rows are recorded as printed. The catalog's Free Electives section prints no fixed figure (the total is determined by the General Education courses taken, degree type, additional credits earned and prerequisite courses needed). Catalog-versus-map difference, disclosed, not reconciled: all three English maps print 'LANG 1020 Intermediate Language I' in Fall Year 2, reusing the code printed in Spring Year 1 for LANG 1020 - Beginning Language II; the slot is recorded as LANG 2010 - Intermediate Language I, the third-semester number in SUU's four-semester language sequence as printed on other official SUU degree maps. Catalog titles are recorded where the map abbreviates or substitutes '&' for 'and'. GE and elective rows printed without course codes are recorded as choice slots with synthetic codes. Cross-check: the catalog's English - Literature Curriculum totals 51 credits (Core Required Courses 6 + Required 3000-Level Surveys 18 + Additional Survey Course 3 + Additional Required Courses 6 + Literature Concentration 18), and the map exercises exactly 51 major credits: all six named Required Surveys appear (ENGL 3210, 3215, 3220, 3230, 3235, 3240), both Additional Required Courses appear (ENGL 4320 and ENGL 4800), the Spring Year 4 'Major Track 3000-Level Survey' slot carries the Additional Survey Course pick (ENGL 3260 or ENGL 3270), and the six generic Major Track elective slots (one lower-division, five upper-division) total exactly the Literature Concentration block's 18 credits. The catalog exercises the Concentration as one of two concentrations (General Literary Studies; Race, Gender, and Culture) whose component lists differ -- a 2000-level course pick (ENGL 2130, 2200, 2210 and, for General Literary Studies, 2230, the 2000-level slot's options), 4000-level literature picks (ENGL 4110, 4210, 4310, 4510, repeatable under different topics) and an additional-course pick (for General Literary Studies ENGL 3860, 4110, 4160, 4210, 4310, 4320 or 4510; for Race, Gender, and Culture a further 4000-level literature course plus one of HIST 3620, HIST 3630, HIST 4760, HIST 4780, LANG 3250, SOC 2630 or WGS 2010) -- so the concentration slots are recorded generically as the map prints them, with both concentrations' lists disclosed here. The map also prints one generic 'GE Elective*' row in Fall Year 2 beyond the named GE breadth rows, recorded as printed.
